title: Independent high-order integration oracle for the frozen fixed-head Layer-ROM ODE
scientific_question: Do the frozen R16_OP Layer-ROM trajectories approach an independently integrated continuous-time solution of the same ODE, and can the B1HCH near-floor exceptions be attributed to finite-step/roundoff behaviour rather than unresolved model-form evidence?

trigger.reason: Four materials show approximately second-order Heun self-convergence, B11 is fully saturated below the frozen identity floor, and B12 has one near-floor nonmonotone storage component. An independent ODE integration route is required before any closure/state redesign.

scope.boundary: fixed zero pressure head at 160 cm, zero top flux
scope.closure: unchanged standard LARE internal closure plus BC1 CURRENT_LAYER_FACE zero-head bottom closure
scope.state: unchanged layer storages plus cumulative boundary bookkeeping

fixed_step_heun.integrator: same source-anchored iterative Heun route used in B1HCG/B1HCH
fixed_step_heun.source: B1HCH implementation and pinned C4V/BC1 basis

oracle_agreement_gate.basis: Numerical resolution gate only, not hydrological acceptance. Compare DOP853_STRICT versus RADAU_STRICT on identical ODE/state.
oracle_agreement_gate.relative_to_existing_B1HCH_mid_fine: For each component, oracle-pair RMS must be <= max(component absolute floor, 0.10 * the immutable B1HCH R16_OP mid-fine RMS self-difference for that material/component).
oracle_agreement_gate.role: Establish that the independent oracle pair is materially tighter than the already observed Heun refinement scale wherever that scale is resolvable.

heun_to_oracle_gate.governing_oracle: DOP853_STRICT, provided the oracle-agreement gate passes
component_rule: Let d1,d2,d3 be pooled RMS differences from Heun dt 1e-4, 5e-5, 2.5e-5 to DOP853_STRICT.

If the immutable B1HCH mid-fine RMS for the component is <= the component absolute floor, classify NUMERICALLY_SATURATED when d3 <= the same absolute floor; no strict monotonicity is required inside that numerical floor.
Otherwise require d2 <= d1 + absolute_floor, d3 <= d2 + absolute_floor, and d3 <= max(absolute_floor, 0.75 * B1HCH_mid_fine_RMS).
heun_to_oracle_gate.expected_order_context: For a second-order asymptotic Heun regime the finest error is approximately one third of the mid-fine difference; the 0.75 multiplier is a preregistered conservative numerical consistency bound, not a hydrological tolerance.
heun_to_oracle_gate.material_supported: all five primary R16_OP components pass either NUMERICALLY_SATURATED or HEUN_APPROACHES_ORACLE

decision_logic: If either independent oracle fails integration/domain checks on any material or the oracle-agreement gate fails on any primary R16_OP component, use B1HCI_INDEPENDENT_ORACLE_NOT_NUMERICALLY_RESOLVED.
Else if all six materials satisfy the frozen Heun-to-oracle material rule, use B1HCI_INDEPENDENT_ODE_ORACLE_SUPPORTS_HEUN_LIMIT_ALL_MATERIALS.
interpretation_rules: Support means the fixed-step Heun research propagator is approaching a stable solution of the unchanged Layer-ROM ODE on the frozen panel. It does not establish that this ODE equals continuous Richards.
If all six are supported while R16_OP retains nonzero finite-Reference residuals, the next causal axis is finite-Reference temporal/discretization contribution, not closure/state redesign.
If the oracle relation is mixed, hold closure/state redesign and diagnose the research propagator or ODE integration domain.
R8 is secondary numerical context and cannot override the R16_OP panel decision.
